description: Motion-direction tuning, feature-based attention (Reynolds & Heeger 2009 Fig 6C). Two same-colour bell curves centred at 0 deg on a LINEAR direction axis. attend_contralateral is the SHARPENED curve: HIGHER at the peak (1.00 vs attend_fixation 0.903, ~0.10 enhancement) but NARROWER (smaller sigma), so it descends faster and CROSSES BELOW attend_fixation on the flanks. Near the peak (|dir|<~36) contralateral is the upper line; the two lines merge in the steep mid-flank (|dir|~35-60) where only the envelope is resolvable; beyond the crossing (|dir|>~60) attend_fixation is the upper (wider) line and attend_contralateral the lower (narrower) line. This crossing IS the feature-based-attention sharpening signature of Fig 6C. NORMALIZATION: larger (contralateral) peak = 1.0 (paper y-axis 'Normalized Response', 0-1); fixation peak ~0.903.

provenance.figure_type: two same-colour bell tuning curves, linear-x, normalized response (0-1); the salient feature is a FLANK CROSSING (sharpening)
tools: per-column dark-pixel CLUSTER tracer (custom; trace_darkest_in_band returns a single path and cannot carry identity through the merge)
provenance.tool_rationale: The two curves are the same colour and merge in the steep mid-flank, so trace_darkest_in_band alone cannot split them or carry identity through the merge. A per-column dark-pixel-cluster trace (excluding the frame top line at rows 6-7 and the baseline) recovers two clusters where the lines separate (near peak and outer flank) and a single envelope cluster where they merge. Curve identity through the merge is fixed by continuity+slope from each apex (the taller contralateral apex descends faster) and verified by matching the re-separated outer-flank clusters to independent Gaussian fits.

calibration.note: detect_plot_box -> (11,6,258,143). Frame top edge at rows 6-7 (val ~1.01) is NOT a curve and was excluded; contralateral apex sits just below it at row 8-9 (val 1.00). Apex at px156 -> deg ~0 (symmetric bell).

per_curve.attend_contralateral: NARROWER/sharpened curve. Traced as the UPPER cluster near the peak (|dir|<~36, apex 1.00). Through the mid-flank merge (|dir|~35-60) only the shared envelope is resolvable. Beyond the crossing it is the LOWER cluster on the outer flank (|dir|>~60). Independent near-peak Gaussian fit: amp ~1.00, sigma ~52.5 deg.
per_curve.attend_fixation: WIDER curve, apex 0.903. LOWER cluster near the peak; shared envelope through the merge; UPPER cluster on the outer flank beyond the crossing. Near-peak Gaussian fit: amp ~0.90, sigma ~61 deg.
per_curve.crossing: The curves CROSS near |dir| ~ 45-60 deg (band-thickness minimum at |dir|~44-48; near-peak Gaussian-fit intersection ~46 deg; clusters resolve as swapped from |dir|~62 deg onward). Near the peak contralateral is upper (gap +0.10 shrinking to 0); on the outer flank fixation is upper (gap ~+0.04). Within the un-resolvable merge band (|dir|~35-60) the two are recorded as coincident (envelope), which is where the geometric crossing falls.

provenance.normalization: paper 0-1 Normalized Response; contralateral peak pinned to 1.0, fixation peak ~0.903 (peak enhancement ~0.097). NOT per-curve normalized.
caveats: No numeric x ticks on the panel; x calibration from the direction-arrow frame (px54=-180, px258=+180). x_range set to +/-175 deg.

Same-colour curves merge in the steep mid-flank (|dir|~35-60 deg, cols 176-190); there only the envelope is recoverable and the two curves are recorded coincident. The crossing falls inside this band, so its exact degree (~45-60) is bounded but not pixel-sharp.

The audit's full-envelope Gaussian fit placed the crossing at ~61 deg; the direct pixel evidence here (band-thickness minimum + near-peak-only Gaussian) places it nearer ~46 deg. Both agree the swap is real; the exact value sits within the merge band and is reported as a range (~45-60 deg).
Curves are symmetrized about 0 deg (right flank traced, left flank mirrored) - the panel is a symmetric bell and the left/right clusters agree.
Far tails (|dir|>~140) the two lines re-converge and are recorded coincident.
